<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914213_theRebbe_9" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914213_theRebbe_9__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Since the year begins, a new chain of descent must be drawn down in a revealed manner from the level of "one," which is above number and relates to the essence of the Ein Sof, enabling all Israel to dwell in one sukkah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">Now,</t>
    <t s="2">since it is the beginning of the year and it is necessary to draw down the entire order of the chain of descent anew, and also in a revealed manner,</t>
    <t s="3">therefore it is necessary to draw down from the aspect of "one."</t>
    <t s="4">And this drawing down</t>
    <t s="5">(in a revealed aspect)</t>
    <t s="6">is done on the day of our festival</t>
    <t s="7">(on the festival of Sukkot)</t>
    <t s="8">as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="9">and therefore the beginning of the service of Sukkot must be in the matter of "one sukkah"</t>
    <t s="10">(that the "one sukkah" is related to the service of Yom Kippur in the three aspects of "one" in the acronym Atz"aN,</t>
    <t s="11">as above),</t>
    <t s="12">for through the service of "one sukkah" one reaches the aspect of "one" that is entirely above even any definition of the concept of number</t>
    <t s="13">(except that since we have no other name to call it, we call it "one"),</t>
    <t s="14">to the Awtsmoos of the Ein Sof, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="15">For "one" means "singular" (Yechidah), as stated in Tosafot,</t>
    <t s="16">and the name "Yechidah" is because it receives from the Singular One (Yachid).</t>
    <t s="17">And likewise is it in the aspect of "one sukkah," whose matter is the concept of Yechidah,</t>
    <t s="18">as above.</t>
    <t s="19">And since the matter of the sukkah has its root in the aspect of "one,"</t>
    <t s="20">therefore it is drawn down below that all Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah,</t>
    <t s="21">for the sukkah is above all division, since its root is in the aspect that is above division.</t>
    <t s="22">And from this very reason, the aspect of "one sukkah" is drawn down even into this lower world, below which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="23">for relative to the Awtsmoos of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, there is no distinction between upper and lower.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The revealed drawing down of Awtsmoos through "one sukkah" will be only in the future, yet even now there is an illumination from it, and it is drawn down specifically through our present service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">a)</t>
    <t s="2">Now,</t>
    <t s="3">the drawing down of Awtsmoos in revelation</t>
    <t s="4">(the aspect of "one sukkah")</t>
    <t s="5">will be only in the future,</t>
    <t s="6">for then it will be, "And the glory of Havayah shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see,"</t>
    <t s="7">and beyond this there will also be, "And your Teacher shall no longer be hidden, and your eyes shall see your Teacher,"</t>
    <t s="8">as stated in Tanya.</t>
    <t s="9">However, above this is the aspect of "one,"</t>
    <t s="10">whose matter is the drawing down of Awtsmoos below in revelation,</t>
    <t s="11">and from this it is understood that the revelation of "one sukkah" will also be only in the future.</t>
    <t s="12">And accordingly, it is understood why our Sages, of blessed memory, derived that all Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah from what is stated at the end of the verse, "all the native-born in Israel," specifically,</t>
    <t s="13">and they did not derive this from the beginning, "In sukkot you shall dwell for seven days,"</t>
    <t s="14">for "In sukkot you shall dwell for seven days" refers to the service in this time, during the six thousand years that the world exists,</t>
    <t s="15">and in this time, the aspect of "one" has not yet been drawn down in revelation.</t>
    <t s="16">And this revelation will be only in the future, and therefore they derived it from what is stated, "all the native-born in Israel,"</t>
    <t s="17">for "native-born" (ezrach) is a future tense term,</t>
    <t s="18">meaning that which will shine forth in the future,</t>
    <t s="19">as explained in many discourses.</t>
    <t s="20">And so it is also according to the rules of grammar, that the letters of the future tense indicate the future.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is, "all the native-born in Israel,"</t>
    <t s="22">that in the future there will be a shining forth of the aspect of "one,"</t>
    <t s="23">and therefore all Israel will then dwell in one sukkah.</t>
    <t s="24">However,</t>
    <t s="25">nevertheless, even now,</t>
    <t s="26">during the six thousand years that the world exists,</t>
    <t s="27">there shines an illumination and radiation from the aspect of "one" that will be revealed in the future.</t>
    <t s="28">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="29">the revelation of the aspect of "one" of the future is drawn down</t>
    <t s="30">(like the other revelations of the future)</t>
    <t s="31">specifically through our deeds and service in the present.</t>
    <t s="32">And from this it is understood that even now there is a semblance and illumination of the aspect of "one."</t>
    <t s="33">And this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said, that all Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah,</t>
    <t s="34">which refers to this time,</t>
    <t s="35">that even in this time there is the matter that all Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah</t>
    <t s="36">(a semblance of the actual dwelling in the future).</t>
    <t s="37">Except that this very thing—that in this time they are fit to dwell—is learned from what is stated, "all the native-born"</t>
    <t s="38">(future tense),</t>
    <t s="39">meaning that the power is taken and drawn from the shining forth that will be in the future,</t>
    <t s="40">which will be the revelation of Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="41">as it is written, "Your Teacher shall no longer be hidden."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The order of service from Rosh Hashanah through Yom Kippur to Sukkot parallels the order of the Torah, which proceeds from general principles to specific details, culminating in the letter Alef of Anochi, which is the inclusive principle of the entire Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">b)</t>
    <t s="2">Now, according to the above, the order of the services of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Sukkot will also be understood.</t>
    <t s="3">And the matter is,</t>
    <t s="4">in the manner of the order in the Torah and the commandments, that general principles and specific details were stated,</t>
    <t s="5">that first matters are in a general manner, and afterward they are drawn into specifics,</t>
    <t s="6">so likewise is the order of the service of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Sukkot.</t>
    <t s="7">For the Torah in its completeness is in a multitude of details,</t>
    <t s="8">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="9">"There are sixty queens and eighty concubines and maidens without number,"</t>
    <t s="10">and our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded</t>
    <t s="11">that "sixty queens" are the Mishnayot,</t>
    <t s="12">"eighty concubines" are the Beraitot, and "maidens without number" are the expositions of our Sages and the sayings of the</t>
    <t s="13">(Tannaim and)</t>
    <t s="14">Amoraim.</t>
    <t s="15">And before this, there is the Torah as it is in the Written Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">as the common expression in the Talmud, "From where are these matters? The verse says."</t>
    <t s="17">For all this is the matter of the Torah as it is in a manner of details and details of details.</t>
    <t s="18">However, there is also the Torah as it is in a general manner,</t>
    <t s="19">that its general principles and its fine details were all stated at Sinai.</t>
    <t s="20">And in the very utterance of the general principles and the specifics,</t>
    <t s="21">first the general principles were stated,</t>
    <t s="22">and afterward the specifics.</t>
    <t s="23">For first the Ten Commandments were stated, in which all the specifics of the Torah are included.</t>
    <t s="24">And the Ten Commandments themselves are included in the utterances "I am" and "You shall not have,"</t>
    <t s="25">as stated in Tanya.</t>
    <t s="26">And these two utterances are included</t>
    <t s="27">in "Anochi," which is the first word of the first utterance.</t>
    <t s="28">And in "Anochi" itself, the letter Alef is its first letter.</t>
    <t s="29">And in this Alef are included all the general principles of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="30">For the letter Alef indicates a matter of generality,</t>
    <t s="31">for it is stated in the Jerusalem Talmud</t>
    <t s="32">that the utterance "Anochi" is hinted at in what is written,</t>
    <t s="33">"Hear O Israel, Havayah is our God,"</t>
    <t s="34">and it is known in the explanation of the word "Echad" (One), that the Chet hints at the seven firmaments and the earth, and the Dalet at the four directions of the world,</t>
    <t s="35">and the Alef before them corresponds to the Holy One, blessed be He, the Master of the world,</t>
    <t s="36">as brought in the Beit Yosef</t>
    <t s="37">from the Sefer Mitzvot Katan,</t>
    <t s="38">as brought and explained in many places.</t>
    <t s="39">And from this it is understood that the Alef of "Anochi"</t>
    <t s="40">(which is related to the "Echad" of "Hear O Israel")</t>
    <t s="41">is the general principle that includes the entire Torah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
